title: Germain's prize essay on elastic surfaces
summary: Self-taught, Sophie Germain worked under a male pseudonym, then on 8 January 1816 became the first woman to win a prize from the Paris Academy of Sciences, for elasticity theory.
why: An early mathematical treatment of vibrating elastic surfaces.

notes.problem: 'Founding work' overclaims: source calls her 'one of the pioneers' and quotes Gray on the work's 'absence of rigor'.

unsung.contribution: One of the pioneers of elasticity theory; won the Paris Academy prize on vibrating elastic surfaces.
unsung.recognition: Poisson published on elasticity without acknowledging her help; some of her results were attributed to Lagrange or rediscovered later.
